title: Russian air strike hits the Donetsk Regional Drama Theatre sheltering civilians in Mariupol
body:
On 16 March 2022, shortly after 10 a.m. local time, an air strike hit the Donetsk Regional Academic Drama Theatre in Mariupol during the siege of the city. Officials said the building was the city's largest air raid shelter and held between 500 and 1,200 civilians, many of them women and children.

Estimates of the number killed differ. Amnesty International said at least a dozen people were killed and that the real number was likely much higher, noting that many had left the building before the attack. The Mariupol City Council gave an early estimate of about 300 dead on 25 March 2022. The Associated Press, in an investigation published on 4 May 2022, estimated about 600 dead. A Russian outlet, Kommersant, reported in April 2022 that at least 11 bodies had been found in the rubble.

The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) reported on 13 April 2022 that it had found no indication for the Russian claim that Azov fighters blew up the theatre and described the incident as most likely an egregious violation of international humanitarian law. Amnesty International concluded on 30 June 2022 that Russian forces carried out the strike using two 500-kilogram bombs and called it a war crime. The Russian Defence Ministry denied responsibility and blamed the Azov Regiment, a claim that independent investigations have not supported, according to the Wikipedia article on the strike.
